headline: Recommended an ordinance updating parking and other citation penalties; approved a motion on the $344,339.40 COVID cost write-off.
summary: Finance staff reported on loan repayments, slower receivables tied to the MUNIS system conversion, and first-month FY27 spending. The $344,339.40 in COVID costs came from a grant that has since closed, and the Fire Department will carry a deficit of about $230,000.
decisions: Accepted the update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund.
Accepted the Finance Department reports on accounts receivable over 90 days, aging, and outstanding receivables.
Approved a motion after discussion of the $344,339.40 COVID write-off; the chair said formal action would come in November.
Accepted the City's Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first month of FY27.
Recommended that the ordinance amendment on parking and other citations pass and be enrolled.

transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATION

October 20, 2026 at 5:15 PM

Chairman O’ Neil called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen O’ Neil, Terrio, Goonan, Burkush, Vincent

Messrs.: Mayor Ruais, K. LeBlanc, M. Bogardus

1. Update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund.

Kim LeBlanc, Financial Analyst II: I have nothing new to add to the report that you have in front of you for the loans. All of them are performing slow, but surely.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted to accept the report.

2. Communication from Kim LeBlanc, Financial Analyst II, submitting Finance Department reports as follows:

- • Accounts Receivable over 90 days
- • Aging Report
- • Outstanding Receivables

K. LeBlanc: There has been a little bit of an increase since the last time we met in July. I have reached out to the airport, DPW, and a few others. Some of it has to do with the conversion to MUNIS. We are still trying to work out some of the bugs, so a lot of the payments are a little bit delayed, and there's some payments due to airport that should be coming in October, so that should decrease when I meet with you again.

Chairman O'Neil: We've seen similar in the past.

K. LeBlanc: Yes. Airport usually has lower revenues for airlines.

On motion of Alderman Terrio , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to accept the reports.

3. Communication from the Financial Analyst requesting to write-off outstanding invoices related to the COVID Disaster Costs incurred by DPW, Fire, and Police in the amount of $344,339.40.

K. LeBlanc: These are costs that were incurred in Covid, but the grant has since closed, so all efforts to receive any more reimbursements on this is done. So we are requesting to write off the $344,000.

Chairman O'Neil: I'm going to go over some notes that I have from Director Wickens that I know you prepared for her. $35,000, Police will absorb in their budget?

K. LeBlanc: Yes.

Chairman O'Neil: And Fire will report back, we'll get a report in the November meeting about the Fire shortfall of about $230,000?

K. LeBlanc: Yes, it will be carrying a deficit in their budget. Hopefully with surplus and revenues in FY 27, it will be a minimal impact.

Chairman O'Neil: And then to my understanding, estimated today, surplus is about $500,000.

K. LeBlanc: That is what Sharon told me. And we also have about $200,000 in contingency if needed.

Chairman O'Neil: Some of that will get made up by unfilled positions in Police and the Assessor. Correct?

K. LeBlanc: Yes.

Chairman O'Neil: So even though we'll end up writing this off in the November meeting, this means Finance is working with the departments on this and seems to have it under control.

Alderman Burkush: We went through Covid, followed all the procedures, and it's important for the public to know that this is not the fault of any particular department or any procedures. It's a change in the policy of the current administration. Is that correct?

Chairman O'Neil: The federal administration. You're absolutely correct. The departments have done nothing wrong. There was a change in procedures and policies at the federal level. You are correct.

Alderman Burkush: Alderman Goonan, you had a lot of experience with that. Any comment on that?

Alderman Goonan: I think all that happened during my tenure there. So you know, during that time, we took directions from the state and federal government on what we could do and what we couldn't do. I think the deficit was basically made up from firefighters that were on the job that became either exposed or infected. And it was the time they had to take off that was required.

Chairman O'Neil: There was a change in the policy that has us having to address it this way.

Alderman Burkush: And then it's also my understanding many communities and the City of Nashua was at $600,000 of unreimbursed money.

Chairman O'Neil: I was not aware of that, but it makes sense. We're accepting the write off in November, correct?

K. LeBlanc: I believe it won't be tonight. It'll be next month.

Mayor Ruais: I did have a conversation with Director Wickens and Chief Cashin about this yesterday. Prior to or when I give my budget address next year, what I can include in my budget is the use of surplus funds to cover the deficit in the department, because that's a larger number than we see in the other ones, we would not ask them to eat those costs within the department. What we would do is we would utilize surplus from next year to cover that. I just wanted to put that on the record so the Fire Department understood that as well, that the intent here is to utilize surplus next year to cover that cost.

Chairman O'Neil: Your Honor, my conversation with Director Wickens, everybody is talking to each other. Police, Fire, the Assessors involved because of some unfilled position, so I'm very pleased with all that. It will get there and we'll take the formal action in November.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to approve.

4. Communication from Sharon Wickens, Finance Officer, submitting the City's Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first month of FY27.

Michelle Bogardus, Deputy Finance Officer: This is the first month that we're using the new MUNIS reporting. So for fiscal year 27, the reports may look a little bit different. For expenditures, the average unobligated balance percentage after one month should be 91.66% as a benchmark, and all departments are within 10% of this benchmark, with the exception of Information Systems, and this is due to the large number of contracts they sign at the beginning of each fiscal year. The overall unobligated balance after one month is $185.4 million for 2026. Health insurance costs for 2027 are tracking on budget. There were no retirement payouts for fiscal year 2027 in July, compared to approximately $14,000 a year ago. There is $200,000 remaining in the contingency account as of July 31st, 2026, for the fiscal year 2027. Revenues for the first month of fiscal year 2027 are at $145,000 lower than a year ago. Auto registrations are $187,000 higher and interest income is $185,000 higher than the same period a year ago. Offsetting these increases are school chargebacks coming in lower due to lower billing from DPW. Payments in lieu of taxes are $116,000 lower in fiscal year 2027 right now, and this is due to the timing of the payments; that's normal for these payments. I do want to point out on page 23 of 32 midway down the page, the percentage obligated for city solicitors should be 3.6%, not 360%. There was an error in reporting. Again, we're working through these new Tyler Munis reports and that slipped by us before we corrected it before publishing.

Chairman O'Neil: MUNIS is going okay?

M. Bogardus: It is.

Chairman O'Neil: Still some bugs?

M. Bogardus: It's a lot of work. We're still working through some things during implementation and working with Tyler Munis to get the reports the way we want them to look. So it's a work in progress.

Chairman O'Neil: Support from the vendor?

M. Bogardus: Yes.

On motion of Alderman Burkush , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to accept the report.

5. Ordinance Amendment:

"Amending Section 70.78 Basic Penalty of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Manchester to include updated parking and other citations."

On motion of Alderman Goonan , duly seconded by Alderman Vincent , it was voted that the Ordinance Amendment ought to pass and be Enrolled.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by

Alderman Burkush , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee

- Meeting Start Time: 5:15PM
- Meeting End Time: 5:28PM
- Minutes Prepared By: Michael Intranuovo
